correctness.rationale: All n>=3: exact graph defect computation, first-10 lower bound on every sink-to-source path, explicit bijection f(v)=Q reverse(P) and its inverse, and connected Eulerian augmentation prove matching bounds. State automaton gives A(z) and weighted sink enumeration gives E(z); rational-series algebra yields the formula including n=3,4 exceptions. The extracted standalone verifier reconstructs cyclic witnesses for n=3..16, checks exact coverage, and tests generating coefficients; a separately formulated full-graph integral min-cost-flow solver agrees for these n. Finite checks corroborate but do not replace the quantified proof.

originality.rationale: The proved all-order connected cyclic covering formula for every finite 010-avoiding n-word was not supplied or implied by the inspected exact-once periodic-language u-cycle literature or the separate multi-cycle shortest cover problem. The two earlier related forbidden-trigram equivalence classes 000 and 001 do not cover the 010 orbit under reversal/complementation. Research search did not surface an equal or stronger statement. Historical completeness is not certified, and an incompletely accessible general-cover article remains a stated residual risk.

value.rationale: The optimum is an exact all-n invariant of the natural language with one forbidden binary trigram, a final symmetry orbit distinct from 000 and 001. The nontrivial sink-to-source bijection determines precise additional-window cost and supplies a constructive Eulerian algorithm; this structural theorem is more informative than a finite table and addresses a motivated gap in universal sequencing.
